lessons.title: തല, കൈ — head and hand, matching Tamil closely
lessons.gloss: head and hand — matching Tamil's native pair almost exactly

segments.text: Malayalam's family words (achan, cēṭṭan...) went their own way from Tamil's. Body parts snap right back to the close match you saw in colors and days.
തല (tala) = "head" — matches Tamil talai closely.
കൈ (kai) = "hand" — matches Tamil kai almost exactly.
Both native Dravidian, both close cousins of Tamil's own words — a reminder that Malayalam and Tamil's vocabulary agreement varies concept by concept, not uniformly.

segments.text: What are Malayalam's words for head and hand, and how closely do they match Tamil? (തല tala, കൈ kai — very closely, both native Dravidian.)

segments.text: Before the new one: മ — what does it do?
One character this time. Just one — and you have been saying it for pages without knowing which mark on the page it was.
ത — ta.
It is a consonant, and in this script a consonant is never bare: it comes with an a already in it. So it is not t, it is ta.
You already say these, and every one of them has ത (ta) somewhere inside it:
അതെ — yes (athe — "that [is so]").
എന്ത് — what.
സന്തോഷം santōṣaṁ — joy / pleased to meet you.
താമസിക്കുക tāmasikkuka — to live, to stay.

lessons.title: Chapter 13 checkpoint — head, hand, ത (ta) and ട (ṭa)
lessons.gloss: Chapter 13 checkpoint — head and hand out loud, then ത and ട on the page

needs: your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: you can do this one in the car, but part of it needs your hands. For that part you will want your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now. I will say so again when we reach them, but leave these sections until you have stopped: Script — ത and ട and Writing — from sound.

segments.text: Nothing new here. The two body words out loud first, then the two letters this chapter put on the page.
(Tala; kai.)
How close are they to Tamil's words? (Very close: Tamil talai and kai. Both pairs are native Dravidian, unlike the family words, where Malayalam went its own way.)
തല is tala, "head". Which letter opens it, and what does it carry? (ത, ta: a consonant with its a built in.)
രണ്ട് is raṇṭŭ, "two". Which letter in it carries ṭa? (ട.)
